info.title: JARVIS
info.description: JARVIS - Just A Rather Very Intelligent System

post.description:
Accept a chat message and return the orchestrator-driven response.

Flow: authentication -> origin validation -> validation -> route ->
orchestrator -> structured response. Conversations are called in
under the authenticated owner/session; provider failures map to the
existing structured errors without leaking internals.

Orchestration additions:

- A rejected model proposal (unknown tool, malformed decision or
  arguments, invalid plan) maps to 422; nothing executes.
- A message too large for the orchestrator instruction budget also
  maps to 422 and is never silently truncated.
- A policy-denied tool proposal maps to 403 (fail closed).
- An unavailable approval store maps to 503 (fail closed, nothing
  executes).

get.description:
List the authenticated identity's conversations (metadata only).

Ordering is ``updated_at DESC, conversation_id DESC``: paginating
again returns the same rows in the same order unless state changed,
and the most recently active conversation is always the first entry
of page one. The page and ``total`` come from ONE consistent
storage transaction.

get.description:
List the authenticated identity's approval records (metadata only).

Strictly read-only: no cleanup, no lazy expiration, no claim, no
state transition. Statuses are persisted verbatim (advisory), the
ordering is ``created_at DESC, approval_id DESC``, and page rows
plus ``total`` come from ONE consistent storage transaction. Raw
arguments, digests, and retention flags are never included. A
corrupted persisted record fails closed with a structured 500.

get.description:
List the authenticated identity's plans (metadata only).

Strictly read-only: statuses and attention flags describe plans
exactly as persisted — no reconcile, no state transition, no
approval side effect. Ordering is ``created_at DESC, plan_id DESC``
and page rows plus ``total`` come from ONE consistent storage
transaction. A corrupted persisted plan fails closed with a
structured 500 instead of being served or skipped.

get.description:
Return the session's plan after approval reconciliation.

The authoritative read: approval-driven states are reconciled on
read and deterministic derived status is added (overall_status,
ready_step_ids, attention lists — Phase 5.2-c). A corrupted
persisted plan fails closed with a structured 500; unknown and
foreign plans observe 404, never the record's state.

post.description:
Request one ready plan step through policy and the approval workflow.

Read-only tools execute once and resolve the step. Mutating tools
return a pending exact-argument approval (202) and execute nothing
here. No automatic advancement happens for other steps.

schema.title: Response Request Plan Step Api Plans  Plan Id  Steps  Step Id  Request Post

post.description:
Explicitly reconcile a RECOVERY_REQUIRED step.

Approval-driven automatic execution never resolves uncertain steps:
whether the side effect occurred cannot be proven by the backend, so
a human acknowledges the uncertainty here. The step resolves FAILED
with an ``execution_uncertain`` classification and the standing
mutation boundary attempt is finalized RECONCILED. The user must
verify any external effect manually; dependents stay blocked either
way until a new plan captures the follow-up work.

ChatResponse.title: ChatResponse
ChatResponse.description:
Chat response contract.

Backward compatible with the Phase 2/3 contract:

- ``status="success"`` — a conversational reply (optionally with the
  structured outcome of an auto-executed read-only tool in
  ``tool_result``).
- ``status="action_proposed"`` — a mutating action was proposed;
  ``action`` carries the exact pending approval. Nothing executed.
- ``status="plan_proposed"`` — a validated multi-step plan was
  captured; ``plan`` carries the steps. Nothing executed.

PlanDetail.title: PlanDetail
PlanDetail.description:
The authoritative plan detail plus deterministic derived status.

Everything from ``TaskPlan`` is served by the existing fields; the
five added fields are derived on read by
``plan_service.derive_plan_status`` from persisted step state and
are never persisted. The listing-side summary (``PlanSummary``)
exposes the same attention flags generated by
``summarize_plan_steps``; the detail is the authoritative read that
also reconciles approval-driven states.

PlanStepStatus.title: PlanStepStatus
PlanStepStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one plan step.

COMPLETED means a successful policy-allowed execution whose
ToolResult is recorded on the step; EXECUTED means an approved
action ran successfully and its ToolResult was recorded by the
approval-outcome listener. FAILED covers every other terminal
outcome and always carries its recorded result. Only recorded
outcomes count for dependency readiness — status alone never proves
success.

RECOVERY_REQUIRED marks a mutating step whose outcome could not be
proven (e.g. the process died after the tool started, or a mutating
execution exceeded its time budget). It is deliberately NOT
terminal: whether the side effect occurred is unknown, so automatic
reporting of success or failure would be dishonest. It resolves only
through explicit reconciliation (resolve-recovery endpoint) to a
FAILED step with an ``execution_uncertain`` result, and it can never
satisfy dependency readiness.
